messages:
Sarah L.: Heads up — opened a docs PR to add an Envoy-based egress example for Private/VPC installs where KMS sits behind a NAT + internal CA. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1234 :memo:

Devon M.: Nice. Can you add a minimal Envoy filter + TLS context snippet? We need clear guidance for validating the cert chain from an internal CA.

Sarah L.: Done — pushed two snippets to the PR. Key pieces included:

- Envoy upstream TLS context (validation_context with concatenated CA bundle)
- systemd unit example to auto-restart redwood-agent if KMS becomes unreachable
- quick `curl` test for mutual TLS health checks

Example envoy config excerpt I added:

```yaml
static_resources:
  clusters:
  - name: kms_upstream
    connect_timeout: 5s
    type: STRICT_DNS
    lb_policy: ROUND_ROBIN
    tls_context:
      common_tls_context:
        tls_certificates:
          - certificate_chain: { filename: "/etc/redwood/certs/client.crt" }
            private_key: { filename: "/etc/redwood/certs/client.key" }
        validation_context:
          trusted_ca:
            filename: "/etc/redwood/certs/ca_bundle.pem" # root + intermediates concatenated
```

Tayla (docs): Pinged for copy edits. Also can we include a short troubleshooting checklist for common cert-chain errors (partial chain, wrong order, missing intermediate)?

Lee: Quick diff suggestion — add this curl command to the troubleshooting section to verify the full chain is accepted by KMS:

```
curl --cert client.pem --key client.key --cacert ca_bundle.pem https://kms.internal.example.com/health
```

Sarah L.: Added the curl example and an `openssl s_client` troubleshooting snippet:

```
openssl s_client -connect kms.internal.example.com:443 -showcerts -CAfile ca_bundle.pem
```

Also added an nftables DNAT example for installs that need to forward egress through a NAT gateway and a note about preserving SNI in Envoy to avoid upstream TLS mismatches.

Devon M.: Can we explicitly call out that Envoy's `validation_context` expects the trusted CAs in a single file (full chain) and that missing intermediates lead to `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`? Small example would help.

Tayla (docs): I'll standardize the wording and add a "What to check" bullet list (order of certs, permissions, CA bundle location, env var KMS_CA_PATH). Also tagging infra to run a smoke test on a private cluster.

Infra Bot: smoke-test triggered for docs-pr-1234 — env-tests/egress-kms — status: queued

Lee: One more tiny addition: systemd unit snippet we should recommend for the agent so it restarts on transient network/KMS failures:

```
[Unit]
Description=Redwood Agent
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/redwood-agent --config /etc/redwood/config.yaml
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Sarah L.: Included that. Also added a note for air-gapped installers: include the `ca_bundle.pem` inside the installer tarball and set `KMS_CA_PATH=/etc/redwood/certs/ca_bundle.pem` in the packaged env. Mentioned file perms (private key must be `chmod 600`).

Devon M.: LGTM aside from one nit about clarifying ownership of the cert files (`chown root:root`). :thumbsup:

Tayla (docs): I'll merge once infra smoke passes and patch the wording nit inline.

Infra Bot: smoke-test status: passed ✅ — env-tests/egress-kms — run-789

Tayla (docs): Merged — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1234 — thx team :tada:

Sarah L.: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with a short KB article for Support with the troubleshooting checklist so they can quickly handle cert-chain tickets.
